overview: AstraZeneca is a global, science-led biopharmaceutical company that researches, develops, manufactures and commercialises prescription medicines across Oncology, BioPharmaceuticals (Cardiovascular/Renal/Metabolism, Respiratory & Immunology, and Infectious Disease) and Rare Disease (Alexion). Headquartered and tax-resident in the UK with major R&D and manufacturing hubs in the US, UK, Sweden and China, the group sells in more than 125 countries and generated $58.7bn of Total Revenue in FY2025. Since February 2026 its ordinary shares trade on a harmonised listing across London, Stockholm and (replacing Nasdaq ADSs) the New York Stock Exchange.

business_model.summary: AstraZeneca earns the large majority of revenue from Product Sales of patented, prescription-only medicines sold through wholly-owned local marketing companies and distributors, supplemented by Alliance Revenue (profit/royalty sharing with partners such as Daiichi Sankyo on Enhertu/Datroway and Sanofi on Beyfortus/Tezspire) and smaller Collaboration Revenue (milestones on legacy out-licensed products like Farxiga/Crestor). Growth is driven by volume uptake of a broadening portfolio of 16+ blockbuster medicines (>$1bn annual sales each) rather than a single dominant drug, with Oncology now the largest and fastest-growing therapy area (44% of FY2025 revenue).

revenue_streams.name: Oncology (Tagrisso, Imfinzi, Enhertu, Calquence, Lynparza, Datroway)
BioPharmaceuticals - Respiratory & Immunology (Symbicort, Fasenra, Breztri, Tezspire)
Rare Disease / Alexion (Ultomiris, Soliris, Strensiq, Koselugo)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/institutional - national healthcare systems, insurers, hospitals and pharmacy benefit managers, prescribed by physicians (ultimate end-user is the patient); some direct-to-consumer discount access via TrumpRx.gov in the US from 2026
business_model.geographic_mix: US 43% of Total Revenue, Europe 22%, Emerging Markets (incl. China) 27%, Established Rest of World (Japan, Canada, Australia, NZ) 9% (H1 2026); US revenue expected to reach ~50% of Total Revenue by 2030; China alone ~11% of Total Revenue

competitive_position.market_position: Top-5 global biopharma by revenue; global leader in lung cancer (Tagrisso, Imfinzi) and a top-3 player in antibody-drug conjugates (Enhertu, Datroway) alongside Daiichi Sankyo, Pfizer/Seagen and AbbVie; leading complement-inhibitor franchise in rare disease via Alexion (Ultomiris/Soliris); a comparatively late entrant into the obesity/GLP-1 market being built via in-house pipeline (AZD5004, AZD6234) and licensing (CSPC, SixPeaks Bio)

moat_factors.description: Deep late-stage oncology and ADC pipeline (197 development projects, 100+ ongoing Phase III studies) built on internal discovery plus bolt-on licensing, generating first-/best-in-class positioning in several tumour types
16 blockbuster medicines across four therapy areas and >80 countries reduce single-product/single-geography concentration risk versus smaller peers
217 on-time launches in 2025, 99%+ supply performance and deep regulatory relationships across US/EU/China/Japan support rapid, broad roll-out of approvals

Co-development and co-commercialisation deals (Daiichi Sankyo, Sanofi, Ionis, Summit Therapeutics, CSPC) de-risk R&D spend and extend reach, but also means a meaningful and growing share of revenue (Alliance Revenue, +31% H1 2026) is split with partners
Two strategic R&D centres (incl. new $2.5bn Beijing centre) and long local presence support access to the world's second-largest pharma market, though volume-based procurement caps pricing upside

weaknesses: Late and currently sub-scale position in the fast-growing GLP-1/obesity category versus Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, requiring costly catch-up licensing and Phase II/III investment
Near-term patent cliff and loss-of-exclusivity exposure, particularly Farxiga in the US (down double digits in CVRM H1 2026) and Brilinta
High and rising Alliance Revenue profit-share to partners compresses consolidated gross margin as newer launch products (Enhertu, Datroway, Tezspire) scale
Significant single-country revenue exposure to US pricing/policy (MFN/TrumpRx, IRA negotiated prices) and to China volume-based procurement
Elevated financial leverage (~$27bn net debt at H1 2026) following the Alexion acquisition and ongoing heavy capex/business-development spend

growth_drivers: Oncology pipeline depth: continued share gains for Tagrisso, Imfinzi, Calquence, Enhertu and rapid ramp of newer launches Datroway and camizestrant/Etcamah, plus >20 high-value Phase III readouts expected over the next 18 months
Rare Disease/Alexion franchise: Ultomiris conversion from Soliris, Strensiq and Koselugo growth, and new indications (e.g., Wainua/Beyonttra in ATTR-CM/ATTRv-PN, Ultomiris in IgAN/gMG)

Obesity/cardiometabolic pipeline: baxdrostat in hypertension/CKD (positive Phase III BaxHTN, now approved in the US as Baxfendy), laroprovstat in dyslipidaemia, and the obesity/T2D portfolio (AZD5004, AZD6234, CSPC collaboration, SixPeaks Bio acquisition) targeting the 2.5bn people living with obesity/overweight

Emerging markets and China: Emerging Markets ex-China revenue +19% actual (FY2025) and a new Beijing R&D centre and CSPC/Alteogen partnerships broaden China-specific pipeline access despite VBP pricing pressure

US manufacturing/tariff hedge: $50bn US manufacturing and R&D investment (incl. $4.5bn Virginia and $2bn Maryland facilities) secures a 3-year Section 232 tariff exemption and supports the ambition for the US to reach ~50% of Total Revenue by 2030

Business development: bolt-on licensing and M&A (EsoBiotec cell-therapy platform, Dizal's Zegfrovy, Sino Biopharmaceutical respiratory licence, $2bn Summit Therapeutics stake/ivonescimab collaboration) continuously refreshes the pipeline
Management's $80bn Total Revenue by 2030 ambition (vs. $58.7bn FY2025), implying a high-single-digit to low-double-digit multi-year CAGR

business.description: Farxiga lost US market exclusivity in 2025/2026 just as its Medicare Maximum Fair Price took effect; Calquence's Maximum Fair Price takes effect 2027; further LOE events will recur across the portfolio over the decade

CARDIO-TTRansform (Wainua in ATTR-CM) missed its primary endpoint in July 2026, and other late-stage trials (EMERALD-2, TMA-313, CAPItello-280/281, LATIFY) have also failed or been discontinued in the past year, illustrating binary pipeline risk across >100 ongoing Phase III studies

Revenue is ultimately dependent on reimbursement decisions by government health systems and insurers; US agreement with the Trump administration and TrumpRx direct-to-consumer pricing could compress realised net prices

business.risk: Late entry to high-growth obesity market
business.description: Competing against incumbents Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly with assets still in Phase IIb, requiring continued catch-up investment/licensing spend with uncertain payoff

financial.description: Net debt rose to $26.9bn at H1 2026 (from $23.4bn at FY2025) on continued M&A, capex and business-development spend, increasing interest-rate sensitivity
Revenue and costs span USD, GBP, SEK, EUR, CNY and other emerging-market currencies; CER vs actual-rate growth regularly diverges by several percentage points

H1 2026 capex of $1.5bn plus a $1.1bn upfront payment to CSPC and the subsequent $2bn Summit Therapeutics investment and $600m Dizal upfront reduce free cash flow available for debt paydown/buybacks in the near term

regulatory.risk: US Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) drug-price negotiation
regulatory.description: Farxiga (first round) and Calquence (second round) selected for Medicare Maximum Fair Price negotiation; more products will likely be added in future negotiation rounds, structurally capping US list-price growth

October 2025 agreement with the US administration ties AstraZeneca to international reference pricing for Medicaid and direct-to-consumer discounts of up to 80% via TrumpRx.gov from 2026, pressuring US net pricing in exchange for a 3-year tariff exemption

regulatory.risk: China volume-based procurement (VBP) and pricing reform
regulatory.description: VBP cycles compress unit prices for mature medicines in China even as volumes/market access expand
Governments and payers are increasingly seeking to limit IP protections globally to manage healthcare costs, risking earlier generic/biosimilar competition

Ongoing commercial litigation, anti-bribery/anti-corruption and pricing-related governmental investigations across multiple jurisdictions (Note 30 of FY2025 accounts) could result in fines or reputational damage

macro.description: US-China strategic rivalry, tariff risk on pharmaceutical imports, and supply-chain disruption are explicitly flagged as a Principal Risk; mitigated partly by the $50bn US manufacturing build-out and the 3-year tariff exemption
Slower-growing government/insurer healthcare budgets amid fiscal constraints create downward pressure on pricing and reimbursement even as underlying demand grows
USD-reporting group with material non-USD revenue/cost bases; a stronger USD is a modest translation headwind to reported (though not CER) growth

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global pharmaceutical sales grew 10.0% in 2025 (IQVIA) and global healthcare spending is projected to grow at a 7.1% annual rate 2025-2029; demand is underpinned by ageing populations, rising chronic disease (cardiometabolic, respiratory, oncology) burden and continued innovation in biologics/ADCs/gene therapies, though offset by payer cost-containment
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low - pharmaceutical demand is largely non-discretionary and defensive relative to the broader economy, though company-specific revenue is sensitive to patent expiries, trial outcomes and policy/pricing decisions rather than the economic cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - ~$32bn gross debt and ongoing debt-funded M&A/capex make net finance expense sensitive to rate moves; investment-grade credit ratings support access to capital markets
key_input_costs: Clinical trial and R&D costs (24% of Total Revenue)
Active pharmaceutical ingredients and biologics manufacturing inputs

recent_developments.event: AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo invested $2bn in Summit Therapeutics (convertible preferred shares, ~10-12% stake) and entered a clinical collaboration to combine Datroway with Summit's ivonescimab, starting with a Phase III trial in 1st-line triple-negative breast cancer

Interim results for H1/Q2 2026: Total Revenue $30.7bn (+9% actual, +6% CER), Core EPS $5.21 (+12%); FY2026 guidance reconfirmed (mid-to-high single-digit Total Revenue growth, low-double-digit Core EPS growth, 18-22% core tax rate); disclosed Dizal Pharmaceutical ($600m upfront + up to $900m milestones) and Sino Biopharmaceutical/CTTQ licensing deals

CARDIO-TTRansform Phase III trial of Wainua (eplontersen) in ATTR-CM missed its primary composite cardiovascular endpoint versus placebo; shares of AZN and partner Ionis fell on the news, though a standalone-therapy subgroup showed a nominally significant benefit pending further analysis

AstraZeneca completed a harmonised global listing, with ordinary shares and debt securities beginning direct trading on the NYSE (ticker AZN) on 2 February 2026 alongside existing London and Stockholm listings, replacing the prior Nasdaq ADS structure; shareholders approved the move 99.36% in favour at a November 2025 general meeting

AstraZeneca reached a Most-Favoured-Nation pricing agreement with the Trump administration, covering Medicaid MFN pricing and future TrumpRx.gov direct-to-consumer discounts (up to 80% on chronic-disease medicines from 2026), in exchange for a 3-year exemption from Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs and a commitment to invest $50bn in US manufacturing and R&D (incl. a $4.5bn Virginia facility and $2bn Maryland expansion)

FY2025 results: Total Revenue $58.7bn (+9%), Reported EPS $6.60 (+45%), Core EPS $9.16 (+12%); 16 positive Phase III readouts and 12 first LCM approvals; full-year dividend raised 3% to $3.20/share; completed acquisitions of EsoBiotec (cell-therapy platform, up to $1bn) and SixPeaks Bio (obesity antibody, buyout of remaining shares); announced new $2.5bn Beijing R&D centre and CSPC Pharmaceuticals obesity/T2D collaboration (announced Jan 2026)

items.notes: Reconfirmed at CER based on average FX rates through 2025; a low single-digit positive FX tailwind to actual growth anticipated if July-Dec 2026 rates hold at June 2026 levels
FX impact on Core EPS growth expected to be broadly similar to the CER growth rate
H1 2026 effective core tax rate was 18%, within range

Management explicitly frames the ambition as assuming 'successes and setbacks' (e.g., absorbing the CARDIO-TTRansform miss) rather than a guaranteed outcome; FY2025 revenue of $58.7bn implies continued high-single to low-double-digit CAGR needed through 2030

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Pascal Soriot highlighted strong H1 2026 performance and continued pipeline delivery (six positive Phase III programmes, eight first approvals in major markets including US approval of Baxfendy for hypertension), said the company is 'disappointed' by the CARDIO-TTRansform outcome but remains on track for the $80bn 2030 ambition, citing more than twenty high-value readouts due over the next 18 months. CFO commentary in the FY2025 report emphasized continued investment across R&D, business development and capex while managing the balance sheet and risk as the highest capital-allocation priority.

bull_case: Deep, catalyst-rich late-stage pipeline (100+ ongoing Phase III trials, >20 high-value readouts over the next 18 months) with oncology (Enhertu, Datroway, camizestrant) and Alexion rare-disease franchises still compounding at double-digit rates

Management's explicit $80bn-by-2030 Total Revenue ambition, with the US pricing/tariff deal and $50bn US manufacturing commitment removing a major tail-risk overhang (tariffs) while securing continued US market access

Successful diversification away from reliance on any single blockbuster — 16 products each generating >$1bn — reduces the impact of any one patent cliff or trial failure (illustrated by the CARDIO-TTRansform miss being absorbed without guidance change)
Emerging markets ex-China growing materially faster (~19-22% CER in FY2025) than developed markets, providing a long runway as healthcare spending in populous nations rises
New harmonised NYSE/LSE/Stockholm listing structure broadens the investor base and could support valuation re-rating versus UK-only large caps
Progressive dividend policy ($3.20/share FY2025, raised H1 2026 interim) supported by strong operating cash generation ($14.6bn FY2025)
bear_case: Binary clinical trial risk is material and recurring — CARDIO-TTRansform, EMERALD-2, CAPItello-280/281 and other Phase III failures in the past year show that a meaningful share of pipeline value is at risk of simply not materializing
US drug-pricing policy (IRA Medicare negotiation on Farxiga/Calquence, MFN/TrumpRx commitments) structurally caps US net pricing just as the US is targeted to become ~50% of revenue by 2030
Farxiga and other CVRM products are now past peak, in US loss-of-exclusivity, creating a revenue headwind that must be continuously offset by new launches

Late and sub-scale position in the obesity/GLP-1 market versus Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly means AstraZeneca may be paying up (CSPC, SixPeaks Bio, business development) for exposure to a market already dominated by larger, more advanced competitors

Rising net debt (~$26.9bn at H1 2026) and heavy ongoing cash outflows for business development (Summit Therapeutics $2bn, Dizal $600m+, CSPC $1.1bn upfront) could constrain capital flexibility if a larger downside pipeline or macro shock occurs
China volume-based procurement and broader global payer cost-containment create a persistent pricing headwind across the ex-US emerging-markets growth engine
